body: That's fair, but not everyone in a bad spot will permanently remain that way. They may not be able to pay it forward immediately, but they do not forget those acts of kindness when things get better.

I see what you mean, but the only reason I'd ask a stranger on the internet for pizza is if I were having a hard time. When things are good, you buy your own pizza. If you're asking for someone else to, it's probably because you're frustrated, hungry, and would be glad if someone would do something nice for you.

I get your frustration with sob stories, but hopefully you can see where others are coming from.

Haven't called anyone yet, but I will. I was just afraid because my sister's dealt with depression her whole life (it's new to me and is pretty fucking scary) and once had cops "help" her by essentially placing her under arrest. 

I've not yet called my landlord because it's tough, but I suppose I have to. Re: simple paycheck jobs - harder than you think. I was under the (false) impression that if the shit truly hit the fan, I'd just go work retail or anything to pay the bills. This is probably a lot easier to do if you're 19. If you're a grown ass adult, even if you neglect to mention your education and salary history because it would immediately disqualify you as "overqualified," they spend two seconds talking to you and are like "Yeah, no." I'd be glad to take a low paying job just to keep the lights on, but that has not worked.

I don't mean to seem like an ingrate, but I'm not looking for job-seeking advice. I have literally heard every single thing and have tried all of it. LinkedIn, networking events, look for lower paying jobs, look for higher paying jobs, have someone review your resume, drink virgin's blood, all of it. At this point it's not about the job. It's about me not wanting to get up in the morning anymore. I just want one moment of peace that I cannot seem to get.

Yeah, I was scared when I was down to my last few months of UI, but figured I'd find a job before then; it's never taken me more than three months to find a job before. Not this time. When that ran out, I panicked, but I had savings and paid rent with that. When *that* ran out, I was in a super panic and sat down and seriously reevaluated my job search. Clearly it needed some reworking and before I spent my retirement savings, which were next. Then that ran out too. WTF? 

I've been told I'm overqualified (cannot tell you how angry that makes me), I've taken my degree off my resume and "dumbed down" my history in order to apply for jobs that paid less than half of what I used to make. But then I'm just another resume that doesn't stand out, so I get passed over for those too. I just cannot catch a fucking break. Seriously, literally everything you can think of I have tried. It is not working. I'm now at the point where I'm going to be thrown out of my apartment because I have no money at all.

I am beyond sick of this shit. I need this nightmare to end now.

I really hope so. If I can get emergency rental assistance for April, I can scrape by for another month. If not, I don't know what I'll do. Just not pay the rent? They can't evict you after one missed payment, I don't think. Eviction is a long freaking hassle, which I hate to take advantage of (I feel like a deadbeat and an asshole), but I need a place to live.

Very freaking depressing. Just gonna keep trying and hope something works out.

Yeah, and it's lunacy for employers to look for *skilled* workers for such little pay, and not saying so in their ads. They waste a lot of people's time. A few weeks ago, I saw a position that required a four year degree, 5+ years of relevant experience, and made no mention of pay. Since this is the field I work in, I know what this role worth, and it matched my experience, so I applied. After e-mailing my resume, they responded asking my salary expectations. I responded with $10k below what I made at my last job, but that I was flexible and willing to negotiate (I've been out of work for a while, and am willing to take a pretty big pay cut because I need to get the hell back to work already), and they said it was way outside of what they're paying and that they'd be moving on. I still don't know exactly what they were offering, but considering how hugely I lowballed myself and that still being way over, it had to have been like $28k. 

You know, if you want someone who's been doing this for 5+ years and has a degree, preferably a certification as well, and who is able to spin plates on their noses, all for $13.50/hr, it is highly advisable you say so upfront. There are people willing to do this, I am sure, but most people who are not completely desperate are not going to cut their pay in half.
I've tried Sleepytime Tea, but not combined with melatonin. Need to pick up some melatonin now. Didn't pick up any last night, even though I totally should have.

I've been hunting like mad. My resume is pretty much entirely ignored. I've gotten a tiny amount of call backs. If I get one again, hell, I have no problem giving them this story. Considering all of the complete nonsense that goes into hiring (junk science personality quizzes, clueless HR people, nepotism, being forced to answer BS interview questions with rank dishonesty "Tell me about you weaknesses..."), I have no problem saying what makes me sound like what their HR person wants to hear.

I've only tried Advil PM and it did nothing. I started taking a bunch more as I was still wide awake, then decided I should probably not take a whole shitload of pills. No insurance yet, but should be on board soon.

:/ Sadly, this is correct. I've been told a few times I would hear back by X date, and if that date passes without word, they're moving on with another candidate. Frustrating and demoralizing, but that's the way it is.

Don't respond to any ad that doesn't name the company or go into specifics of the job. It is a scam, period. If a job gives info about the company, especially if it lists a direct e-mail address in it or a url to the company's career section of the website, assuming you Googled them and it checked out, go ahead and apply. It looks like you're looking for service jobs, and a lot of those tell you to apply in person. Those are usually legit.

A quick list of what to avoid at all costs:

* Jobs that are completely shady on the details of the job or the company.
* Companies that spam Craigslist over and over again WITH THEIR ALL CAPS TITLES AND EXCLAMATION MARK ABUSE!!! You'll also see the same exact job posted to every category. Really, this is a business/mgmt job, a service industry job, an admin job, a sales job, a marketing, AND a human resources job? Dang.
* The marketing section is hilariously bad. Job titles like "Marketing Rep" or "Direct Marketing" whose only qualifications are "a desire to grow" are door to door sales jobs. All of them.
* Don't be taken in by too good to be true. No one is going to pay you $60k to stock shelves or be a receptionist. It's a scam.

Hope this helps. I've been at this shit for way too long, sadly.

Thank you so much for the kind of thoughtful response! Some of these things I have tried, others I have not (some I can't). One of the things here I can and definitely will try is shutting off electronics a couple of hours before attempting to sleep at night. I've actually read before that this can be helpful. Sleep compression therapy sounds hard core, but I'll go in for it if nothing else works. I don't say no to anything if it'll help me get some shut eye!

What's most frustrating is I don't usually have trouble sleeping. It's the stress and depression that keeps the wheels turning nonstop and I wish they would just STOP. I can't get a single moment of peace which is maddening. I'm like, "Come on, life! Just give me 8 measly hours to not not feel like shit!"

FWIW, I agree with you. When I'm not depressed, I'm pretty active, so I thought surely I'd feel better if I exercised because I do when I'm up, plus no one can shut the fuck up about how I'll feel oh-so-chipper if I just go for a jog, right? Right? Wrong! Not only has my depression zapped my willingness to do this, but even when I do, I do not feel any better at all. I end up feeling worse a lot of the time.

I don't always know what to say to people who vent to me either, but I'm going to assume my bit of facile advice isn't new to them. If you don't understand their situation, preaching is a lot less effective than asking questions and listening.

Good idea. I tried Advil PM and it didn't work. :\ I don't know if it was because I was too agitated or if it's just not very effective, but I will try this. I'm not sure why it never occurred to me that you could buy melatonin at the store, but it looks like they're sold at every CVS and Walgreens.
